test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 02 Sept, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following was the biggest armed resistance to colonialism in the 19th century in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sepoy Mutiny**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sepoy Mutiny of 1857** (also known as the First War of Independence or the Indian Rebellion of 1857) was the **largest armed resistance** against British colonial rule in the 19th century in India.
 
• The revolt began as a mutiny by Indian soldiers (sepoys) serving in the British East India Company's army but soon escalated into a widespread rebellion involving peasants, landlords, and other sections of society.
 
• The immediate cause of the mutiny was the introduction of the new **Enfield rifle**, the cartridges of which were reportedly greased with cow and pig fat, offending Hindu and Muslim religious sentiments. *Hence, it was a significant catalyst for the rebellion.*
 
• The revolt spread across northern and central India, with major centers of resistance in **Delhi, Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi, and Gwalior**, among others.
 
• The rebellion was characterized by **violent confrontations**, including massacres and retaliatory actions by both the British forces and the Indian rebels. *This marked it as one of the most significant uprisings against colonial rule in India.*
 
• Although the mutiny was eventually suppressed by the British by 1858, it had a profound impact on the colonial administration, leading to the dissolution of the **British East India Company** and the establishment of direct Crown rule in India.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is the Sepoy Mutiny.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **First Anglo-Maratha War:**

 
 
• The **First Anglo-Maratha War** (1775–1782) was fought between the British East India Company and the Maratha Empire. It was not a resistance against colonialism but rather a conflict for territorial and political dominance.
 
• The war ended with the **Treaty of Salbai**, which restored the status quo between the two sides. **It was not the largest armed resistance** to colonial rule in the 19th century.
 
 
 
• **Quit India Movement:**
 
 
• The **Quit India Movement** was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in **1942** during World War II, demanding an end to British rule in India. It was a mass civil disobedience movement but did not involve large-scale armed resistance.
 
• This movement played a crucial role in India's independence struggle but was not a 19th-century event.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Buxar:**
 
 
• The **Battle of Buxar** (1764) was fought between the British East India Company and the combined forces of **Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula, and the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II**. It resulted in the consolidation of British power in Bengal.
 
• While it was an important event in Indian history, it occurred in the 18th century and was not an armed resistance against British colonialism in the 19th century.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact of the Sepoy Mutiny:**

 
 
• The rebellion led to the **end of the East India Company’s rule** and the beginning of direct British Crown administration in India under the Government of India Act 1858.
 
• The mutiny exposed the weaknesses in the British administration and highlighted the discontent among Indian soldiers and the general public under colonial rule.
 
• It also inspired future freedom movements and leaders, becoming a symbol of resistance against colonial oppression.
 
 
 
• **Reasons for Failure:**
 
 
• The lack of a central leadership and coordination among the rebels was a major reason for the failure of the mutiny.
 
• The British had superior military strength and resources, enabling them to suppress the rebellion effectively.
